steps.what: Read the inpatient record before reviewing current care
Examine and treat hospital inpatients at the bedside
Decide the working diagnosis and continuing care priorities
Coordinate current care priorities with the ward team
Write the inpatient progress note in the clinical record

loop.purpose: Draft the progress narrative from the clinician's findings and decisions
loop.input: patient record references and clinician dictation
loop.check: Hospitalist checks chronology, negation, diagnosis uncertainty, treatment intent and omitted findings before writing the final note
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unclear attribution returns to manual documentation
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies headings but cannot turn variable bedside findings into an accurate narrative

tasks.design: Configure a current-patient view in the {OTHER} clinical record, then test a bounded note draft from hospitalist dictation. The hospitalist retains examination, diagnosis, care coordination and correction of the final progress note.
tasks.previous_blocker: The progress narrative had to be composed after reviewing observations and discussing care.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical note drafting is available, while a native patient view can reduce repeated screen navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Rapid deterioration, incomplete histories and conflicting findings require bedside judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a changing clinical condition and taking responsibility for care.
tasks.altitude: A little less retrospective typing; clinical decision rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts clinical consultation notes for clinician validation and clinical-record integration.
The Capio study reported self-estimated note time falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes, with substantial editing remaining; this is context, not a local inpatient-care saving.
The task shares, native-view benefit and inpatient note retention are model knowledge estimates.

assumptions: Boundary is a continuing inpatient review and its progress note. Admission documentation, medication orders and test orders are separately counted in the other tasks in this answer; this task retains their clinical implications but not duplicate order entry.

The {OTHER} category is the clinical patient-record system. Observation value, unit, measurement time, recorder and encounter ID come from existing nursing or laboratory records; their original production is other-role work outside this focal baseline and earns no saving. Hospitalist verification is in s1; missing or stale observations require manual review rather than inferred normal values.

The hospitalist produces findings, decision rationale and patient identity confirmation in s2-s3 and dictates them during s5; capture and correction time remain inside s5's retained 13.75 hours. Unsupported structured fields stay blank and are entered manually.
Test native current-patient views and note headings before any custom integration. The author's ordinary same-system save is included at its negligible real time with no extra approval or saving.
unknowns: Availability of approved clinical note drafting and patient-record access
Actual progress-note typing and editing time

steps.what: Review medications, allergies and current treatment constraints
Choose medications or treatment regimens for this inpatient
Enter the medication or treatment order details
Check the final order and resolve medication surveillance findings
Release the checked prescription to the ward and pharmacy

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} prescribing screen with a medication-and-allergy view and editable, clinically approved favourites. The hospitalist chooses the regimen, resolves existing medication surveillance findings and releases the exact checked order; no additional automated alert or release is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated drug search and field entry interrupt the clinical prescribing decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native prescribing favourites can populate a starting order without choosing the patient's treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Renal function, uncertain allergies, interactions and changing clinical status can invalidate a routine regimen.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a justified treatment and recognising when a default is inappropriate.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive order entry with unchanged prescribing responsibility.

reach.task: Resolve a clinically ambiguous medication discrepancy
reach.learn: Medication reconciliation and formulary change control

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard supports interaction, contraindication, dose and duplicate-medication surveillance; it does not replace the prescriber.
Editable prescribing favourites and their estimated entry-time benefit are model knowledge; local coverage is unconfirmed.

assumptions: Boundary covers prescribing after clinical assessment, not examination or administration. Release is a real clinical instruction to the ward and pharmacy, not an ordinary author save; its small existing time stays fully retained.

The {OTHER} category is the clinical prescribing system. The hospitalist confirms encounter ID, drug, formulation, dose, unit, route, frequency, duration and indication in s3. These fields are not inferred from a diagnosis; manual entry remains the fallback and its time is included in s3.

Allergies, current drugs and dated renal results come from the existing patient record, with original capture by care staff outside this focal denominator. s1 counts hospitalist verification and missing-data clarification; s4 counts review of existing surveillance output. Existing surveillance runtime is system work with no labour saving.
Test native favourites and consolidated views first. No separate gate or saving is attached to a draft's ordinary same-system save.

tasks.design: Configure native test-request favourites and a dated results view in the {OTHER} clinical record. Reuse selected result references in the assessment-entry template, while the hospitalist retains test selection, clinical interpretation, request checking and submission.

tasks.enabler_now: Existing native request lists, result timelines and linked record fields may remove navigation and transcription.
tasks.still_hard: A numeric trend does not establish a diagnosis or determine whether a test was clinically indicated.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting discordant results and deciding what should happen next.

evidence.claim: Native result timelines, request favourites and linked assessment fields are a model knowledge design; no digest case establishes their local time saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes choosing and entering tests, submitting the clinical instruction, reading returned results and writing the specific interpretation. Specimen collection and radiology reporting are other-role work, not savings; generic later progress-note composition in task 17106 excludes this already written result assessment.

The {OTHER} category is the clinical patient-record and ordering system. The hospitalist produces encounter ID, test code, indication, urgency and requested timing in s2 and checks them in s3. Templates leave unsupported details blank; manual order entry is the fallback with capture time retained in s2.

Laboratory and radiology services produce result ID, specimen or acquisition time, value, unit, reference interval, report text and status through existing clinical processes. s5 counts hospitalist retrieval and verification; missing units, mismatched dates or preliminary reports prevent automatic field reuse and require manual reading.

Use native configuration first. Existing result delivery and existing runtime alerts are unchanged and earn no labour saving. s4 is a clinical request release, its full small time retained; ordinary assessment saving has no separate approval stage.

steps.what: Review the referral and establish the incoming patient's identity
Assess the patient's need for a hospital stay
Decide admission suitability and required level of care
Write the admission history and admission decision in the clinical record

loop.purpose: Draft the admission narrative from referral material and clinician dictation
loop.input: identified referral and hospitalist admission findings
loop.output: draft admission history and decision rationale
loop.check: Hospitalist checks identity, history attribution, chronology, negative findings, uncertainty and level-of-care rationale before writing the final note
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; uncertain source identity or missing assessment returns to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Referral prose and bedside histories vary too much for headings alone to compose the narrative

steps.what: Enter the admission status and requested ward in the patient system
Communicate the admission decision and immediate needs to the receiving ward

tasks.design: Use the {OTHER} clinical record's native referral view and admission form, with a bounded draft for the admission narrative. The hospitalist assesses the patient, chooses the care level, corrects the note, enters admission status and hands over to the ward.
tasks.previous_blocker: Admission history is repeatedly retyped from referral material and the clinician's assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical note drafting can compose a source-linked starting narrative; native form context can avoid re-entering verified identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Admission thresholds, uncertain histories and the receiving ward's actual ability to care for the patient.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether admission is appropriate and conveying urgent care needs clearly.
tasks.altitude: Less admission-note typing; admission and placement responsibilities remain with the clinical team.

reach.learn: Ward handover requirements and care-level constraints

evidence.claim: Autoscriber supports clinical note drafting with clinician validation and patient-record integration; inpatient admission performance still requires testing.
Admission-specific shares, field reuse and retained editing time are model knowledge estimates.

assumptions: Boundary includes the admitting hospitalist's referral review, assessment, admission note, status entry and ward handover. Transport, bed allocation and nursing admission work are outside this focal denominator and earn no saving; subsequent progress reviews, prescribing and test orders are separate tasks.

The {OTHER} category is the clinical patient-record system. Referral source, patient identifiers, encounter ID and referral timestamp come from the referring service; s1 counts the hospitalist's identity and provenance verification. Unmatched identifiers require manual reconciliation, never guessed matching.

The hospitalist produces admission findings in s2 and decision, level of care and requested ward in s3. Dictation capture and correction remain inside s4's retained 18 hours; admission status fields are confirmed in s5, which retains 4 hours. Missing details require manual entry, not default admission decisions.

Test native admission forms before custom code. An ordinary author save or native status entry requires no invented approval stage and saves no click time; s5's one-hour potential benefit is identifier re-entry avoided, not saving the record.
unknowns: Whether hospitalists enter admission status themselves
Admission-note drafting permissions and actual editing burden
research_questions: Does admission drafting preserve uncertainty and reduce total note work without delaying handover?
